summary.en: Making a profit and having cash are two different things. This topic shows why.
summary.bs: Imati dobit i imati novac su dvije različite stvari. Ova tema pokazuje zašto.

formula.en: Gross profit = Revenue − Cost of goods sold
formula.bs: Bruto dobit = Prihod − Trošak prodane robe

en.one: Gross profit is what is left from sales after paying for the products themselves.
en.explain: Only the direct costs of what you sold are taken away: materials, stock, production. Rent, salaries for the office and marketing are not taken away yet.
en.example: A shop sells clothes for €10,000 in a month. It paid suppliers €6,000 for those clothes. Gross profit is €4,000.
en.why: It shows if your product itself makes money, before everything else.
en.mixup: Gross profit is not the money you take home. Many costs still have to be paid from it.

bs.one: Gross profit (bruto dobit) je ono što ostane od prodaje kad platiš same proizvode.
bs.explain: Oduzimaju se samo direktni troškovi onoga što si prodao: materijal, roba, proizvodnja. Kirija, plate u kancelariji i reklama se još ne oduzimaju.
bs.example: Prodavnica u mjesecu proda odjeću za 10.000 €. Dobavljačima je za tu odjeću platila 6.000 €. Bruto dobit je 4.000 €.
bs.why: Pokazuje da li sam proizvod donosi novac, prije svega ostalog.
bs.mixup: Bruto dobit nije novac koji nosiš kući. Iz nje se još plaćaju mnogi troškovi.

formula.en: Net profit = Revenue − All costs − Taxes
formula.bs: Neto dobit = Prihod − Svi troškovi − Porezi

en.one: Net profit is what is left after every single cost and tax has been paid.
en.explain: It is the bottom line: the last number on the income statement. Product costs, rent, wages, marketing, interest and taxes are all taken away.
en.example: The shop has €4,000 gross profit. Rent is €1,500, wages €1,800, other costs €300 and taxes €100. Net profit is €300.
en.why: This is the real answer to the question: did the business make money?
en.mixup: Net profit is not the same as cash. You can have net profit on paper and an empty bank account.

bs.one: Net profit (neto dobit) je ono što ostane kad se plati baš svaki trošak i porez.
bs.explain: To je zadnja linija: posljednji broj u bilansu uspjeha. Oduzimaju se troškovi proizvoda, kirija, plate, reklama, kamate i porezi.
bs.example: Prodavnica ima 4.000 € bruto dobiti. Kirija je 1.500 €, plate 1.800 €, ostali troškovi 300 € i porezi 100 €. Neto dobit je 300 €.
bs.why: Ovo je pravi odgovor na pitanje: da li je firma zaradila?
bs.mixup: Neto dobit nije isto što i gotovina. Možeš imati dobit na papiru i prazan račun u banci.

formula.en: Cash flow = Cash in − Cash out
formula.bs: Novčani tok = Novac koji uđe − Novac koji izađe

en.one: Cash flow is the real money moving in and out of your bank account.
en.explain: Positive cash flow means more money came in than went out in a period. Negative means more went out. It follows actual payments, not promises.
en.example: In March you send invoices worth €10,000, but customers pay only €4,000. You pay €6,000 in bills. Your cash flow for March is −€2,000.
en.why: Bills, wages and rent are paid with cash, not with profit. Cash flow keeps the lights on.
en.mixup: A sale is not cash until the customer actually pays.

bs.one: Cash flow (novčani tok) je stvarni novac koji ulazi na tvoj račun i izlazi s njega.
bs.explain: Pozitivan novčani tok znači da je u nekom periodu više novca ušlo nego izašlo. Negativan znači da je više izašlo. Prati stvarne uplate, ne obećanja.
bs.example: U martu pošalješ fakture od 10.000 €, ali kupci plate samo 4.000 €. Ti platiš 6.000 € računa. Tvoj novčani tok za mart je −2.000 €.
bs.why: Računi, plate i kirija se plaćaju gotovinom, a ne dobiti. Novčani tok drži firmu živom.
bs.mixup: Prodaja nije novac dok kupac stvarno ne plati.

concepts.term: Why profitable firms run out of cash
concepts.youtubeQuery: why profitable companies run out of cash

en.one: A business can be profitable and still go broke if the cash arrives too late.
en.explain: Profit is counted when you make a sale. Cash arrives when the customer pays, which can be weeks or months later. Meanwhile you still pay suppliers, rent and wages. Fast-growing businesses are most at risk because they spend first and get paid later.
en.example: A furniture maker wins a big order worth €50,000 with payment in 90 days. To build it, he must pay €30,000 for wood and workers now. On paper he made €20,000. In the bank he is €30,000 short.
en.why: This is one of the most common reasons small businesses close. Watching cash, not just profit, protects you.
en.mixup: Running out of cash does not always mean the business idea is bad. Often it is only a timing problem that better planning could fix.

bs.one: Firma može biti profitabilna i svejedno propasti ako novac stigne prekasno.
bs.explain: Dobit se računa kad prodaš. Novac stiže kad kupac plati, a to može biti sedmicama ili mjesecima kasnije. U međuvremenu i dalje plaćaš dobavljače, kiriju i plate. Firme koje brzo rastu su najugroženije, jer prvo troše, a kasnije naplate.
bs.example: Stolar dobije veliku narudžbu od 50.000 € s plaćanjem za 90 dana. Da je napravi, mora odmah platiti 30.000 € za drvo i radnike. Na papiru je zaradio 20.000 €. U banci mu fali 30.000 €.
bs.why: Ovo je jedan od najčešćih razloga zašto se mali biznisi zatvaraju. Kad pratiš novac, a ne samo dobit, štitiš se.
bs.mixup: Kad ponestane novca, to ne znači uvijek da je ideja loša. Često je to samo problem vremena koji bolje planiranje može riješiti.
